stem: Laryngitis is defined as inflammation of which structure?
options: The larynx (voice box)
The pharynx only
The trachea only
The epiglottis exclusively

stem: The characteristic swelling of laryngitis affects which structures, resulting in hoarseness and voice changes?
options: The vocal cords
The tonsils
The adenoids
The thyroid gland

stem: Beyond hoarseness, which combination of symptoms is also characteristic of laryngitis?
options: Loss of voice, sore throat, and a dry cough
Severe abdominal pain and vomiting
Painless swelling of the ankles
Sudden loss of hearing

stem: At what duration does laryngitis begin to be classified as chronic rather than acute?
options: More than three weeks
More than three days
More than three hours
More than three months

stem: Acute laryngitis is typically characterized by which onset and course?
options: Sudden onset, often due to viral infections, typically resolving within a few days to three weeks
Gradual onset over several years with no identifiable trigger
Onset exclusively in neonates, never in adults
An onset that always requires surgical intervention within 24 hours

stem: Acute laryngitis is most commonly associated with which clinical context?
options: Upper respiratory tract infections, being usually self-limiting
Lower gastrointestinal infections
Chronic kidney disease
Peripheral vascular disease

stem: Chronic laryngitis is most strongly associated with which pattern of exposure?
options: Prolonged exposure to irritants such as smoking, environmental pollutants, or gastroesophageal reflux
A single, brief viral illness lasting less than 24 hours
One-time exposure to cold air during a single winter day
Strict avoidance of all vocal activity for more than a year

stem: Chronic laryngitis may cause which lasting change, distinguishing it from most cases of acute laryngitis?
options: Lasting changes in vocal cord structure and function
Complete and permanent loss of the sense of smell
Permanent paralysis of the diaphragm
Irreversible loss of taste buds on the tongue

stem: Among infectious causes of laryngitis, which category is described as the MOST common?
options: Viral causes, including rhinovirus, influenza virus, parainfluenza, and adenovirus
Bacterial causes, including Streptococcus pneumoniae
Fungal causes, including Candida species
Parasitic causes, including intestinal helminths

stem: Which bacterial organisms are specifically listed as LESS common infectious causes of laryngitis?
options: Streptococcus pneumoniae and Haemophilus influenzae
Rhinovirus and adenovirus
Candida species exclusively
Mycobacterium tuberculosis exclusively

stem: Fungal laryngitis, caused by Candida species, is particularly associated with which patient population or exposure?
options: Immunocompromised individuals or those with prolonged corticosteroid inhaler use
Healthy young athletes with no medication use
Patients who have never used any inhaled medication
Patients with a recent uncomplicated viral cold only

stem: Vocal overuse or misuse, such as excessive shouting or singing, is classified as which type of cause of laryngitis?
options: A non-infectious cause
A viral infectious cause
A bacterial infectious cause
A fungal infectious cause

stem: Besides vocal overuse, which lifestyle factors are listed among the non-infectious causes of laryngitis?
options: Smoking and alcohol consumption
Regular moderate exercise
Adequate daily water intake
Routine annual dental checkups

stem: Which digestive condition is specifically listed as a non-infectious cause of laryngitis?
options: Gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD)
Irritable bowel syndrome
Peptic ulcer disease unrelated to reflux
Appendicitis

stem: Allergies and post-nasal drip are classified under which category of laryngitis causes?
options: Non-infectious causes
Viral infectious causes
Bacterial infectious causes
Fungal infectious causes

stem: Which autoimmune conditions are specifically listed as non-infectious causes of laryngitis?
options: Rheumatoid arthritis and sarcoidosis
Type 1 diabetes mellitus and Hashimoto's thyroiditis
Systemic lupus erythematosus and multiple sclerosis
Celiac disease and Crohn's disease

stem: Which occupational group is specifically identified as being at higher risk for laryngitis due to high vocal demand?
options: Teachers, singers, and public speakers
Accountants and data entry clerks
Night-shift security guards
Long-distance truck drivers

stem: Where is the larynx located, and what structures does it house?
options: In the upper part of the respiratory tract, housing the vocal cords
In the lower gastrointestinal tract, housing the appendix
In the middle ear, housing the ossicles
In the abdominal cavity, housing the pancreas

stem: In the pathophysiology of laryngitis, inflammation causes swelling and irritation of which structure?
options: The mucosa lining the larynx
The outer skin of the neck only
The cartilage of the external ear
The lens of the eye

stem: This swelling and irritation of the laryngeal mucosa leads to which functional change?
options: Altered vibration of the vocal cords and changes in voice quality
An immediate and complete loss of the gag reflex only
A permanent increase in vocal pitch with no other change
Enhanced, clearer voice production in all cases

stem: Chronic inflammation in laryngitis may lead to which structural changes on the vocal cords, impairing normal phonation?
options: Thickening, nodules, or polyps
Calcification of the entire trachea
Complete absence of the vocal cords
Fusion of the vocal cords with the epiglottis

stem: Which clinical manifestation describes a COMPLETE loss of voice in laryngitis?
options: Aphonia
Dysphagia
Dyspnea
Dysuria

stem: Besides hoarseness and aphonia, which throat-related symptom is characteristic of laryngitis?
options: Dry, scratchy, or sore throat
Severe unilateral ear pain only
Painless swelling of the tongue only
Loss of sensation in the throat only

stem: The dry cough associated with laryngitis is typically described as being worse at which time?
options: At night
Only immediately after waking in the morning
Only during vigorous exercise
Only while eating solid food

stem: Besides a dry cough, which other symptom related to speech is characteristic of laryngitis?
options: Difficulty speaking or vocal fatigue
Sudden, complete paralysis of the tongue
Permanent loss of the ability to swallow liquids
Immediate, irreversible loss of hearing

stem: Swollen lymph nodes in the neck, when seen in laryngitis, are typically associated with which underlying process?
options: An associated infection
A purely non-infectious, allergic cause only
Vocal overuse in the complete absence of any infection
Chronic GERD exclusively, with no infectious component

stem: Fever and malaise, when present in laryngitis, are typically seen in which form of the condition?
options: Infectious forms
Purely non-infectious, vocal-overuse forms only
Purely allergic forms only
Purely GERD-related forms only

stem: Which diagnostic procedure is used to directly visualize the vocal cords and assess for structural abnormalities in laryngitis?
options: Laryngoscopy
Abdominal ultrasound
Electrocardiography
Lumbar puncture

stem: Throat swabs are obtained in the diagnostic workup of laryngitis primarily to identify which type of causative organism?
options: Bacterial or fungal organisms, via culture
Only autoimmune markers
Only serum electrolyte abnormalities
Only blood glucose levels

stem: Imaging studies such as CT or MRI are indicated in the workup of laryngitis when which complication is suspected?
options: Malignancy or a structural issue
A routine, uncomplicated viral cold with no red flag symptoms
Simple, self-limiting acute laryngitis lasting less than one week
A single episode of mild hoarseness with no other symptoms

stem: Referral to an ENT specialist for voice assessment is particularly recommended for which presentation of laryngitis?
options: Chronic or recurrent laryngitis
A single mild episode lasting less than three days
Laryngitis occurring only once in a lifetime with full resolution
Laryngitis that resolves completely within 24 hours without treatment

stem: As part of supportive treatment for laryngitis, what instruction should be given regarding whispering?
options: Patients should avoid whispering, since it strains the vocal cords
Patients should whisper constantly instead of speaking at a normal volume
Whispering has no effect on the vocal cords and may be used freely
Whispering is the preferred method of complete voice rest

stem: Adequate hydration is recommended in laryngitis management for which specific purpose?
options: To thin mucus and soothe irritated mucosa
To directly cure any underlying bacterial infection without antibiotics
To eliminate the need for voice rest entirely
To permanently reverse chronic vocal cord nodules

stem: Humidified air is recommended in laryngitis management to achieve which effect?
options: To help relieve dryness and irritation
To directly kill any viral pathogens present
To permanently increase vocal pitch
To replace the need for any fluid intake

stem: Warm saline gargles are recommended in laryngitis management primarily for which purpose?
options: Throat comfort
Definitive eradication of fungal infection
Permanent structural repair of vocal cord nodules
Replacement of prescribed antibiotic therapy

stem: Which class of medications is recommended in laryngitis for pain and fever control, such as paracetamol or ibuprofen?
options: Analgesics and antipyretics
Antifungals
Proton pump inhibitors
Corticosteroid inhalers exclusively

stem: Antibiotics are indicated in the pharmacological management of laryngitis under which specific condition?
options: Only if bacterial infection is confirmed
In every single case of laryngitis, regardless of cause
Only for cases caused by vocal overuse
Only for cases caused by allergies

stem: Antifungal medications are indicated in laryngitis management for which confirmed cause?
options: Confirmed fungal laryngitis
Confirmed viral laryngitis
Confirmed GERD-related laryngitis
Confirmed vocal-overuse laryngitis

stem: Antihistamines, used in allergy-induced laryngitis, must be used with which precaution?
options: Cautiously, to avoid drying the mucosa
Only in combination with high-dose corticosteroids at all times
Without any precaution, as they have no drying effect
Only intravenously, never orally

stem: Proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) are indicated in laryngitis management when the cause is related to which condition?
options: Gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD)
Viral upper respiratory infection
Vocal cord nodules from overuse alone
Allergic rhinitis alone

stem: Corticosteroids, used short-term in laryngitis, are indicated for which situations?
options: Severe inflammation or professional voice users
Mild, self-limiting cases requiring no other treatment
Confirmed fungal laryngitis as first-line therapy
Routine prophylaxis in all patients regardless of severity

stem: Surgical management of laryngitis is reserved for which specific situations?
options: Persistent structural lesions such as nodules, polyps, or granulomas affecting the vocal cords
Every single case of acute viral laryngitis
Mild hoarseness lasting less than three days
Uncomplicated allergy-induced laryngitis responding to antihistamines

stem: In the nursing assessment of a patient with laryngitis, which vocal parameters should be monitored?
options: Voice quality, frequency, and duration of symptoms
Only the patient's handwriting legibility
Only the patient's gait pattern
Only the patient's appetite for solid food

stem: A critical safety component of nursing assessment in laryngitis is evaluating for which potentially serious signs?
options: Signs of airway obstruction, stridor, or respiratory distress
Signs of ingrown toenails
Signs of seasonal hay fever only
Signs of mild sunburn

stem: Besides monitoring voice and airway status, nursing assessment in laryngitis should also evaluate which physiological parameter?
options: Hydration status and fluid intake
Visual acuity using a Snellen chart
Deep tendon reflexes in the lower limbs
Peripheral pulses in all four limbs

stem: Nursing assessment in laryngitis should also include identifying and documenting which information?
options: Possible causative or exacerbating factors
The patient's preferred television programme
The patient's choice of clothing colour
The patient's favourite type of music

stem: Which nursing intervention directly addresses vocal strain in a patient with laryngitis?
options: Encouraging complete voice rest and educating the patient to avoid whispering and throat clearing
Encouraging the patient to shout loudly to 'exercise' the vocal cords
Encouraging frequent, prolonged singing sessions
Encouraging constant whispering as a substitute for normal speech

stem: Which nursing intervention helps ease breathing and soothe the throat in a patient with laryngitis?
options: Providing humidified oxygen or using a room humidifier
Administering dry, unheated, low-humidity air exclusively
Restricting all fluid intake to less than 500 mL per day
Encouraging the patient to breathe exclusively through the mouth in cold, dry air

stem: Which type of fluids are specifically recommended as a nursing intervention to encourage intake in laryngitis?
options: Warm fluids, such as herbal teas and soups
Ice-cold carbonated beverages exclusively
Caffeinated energy drinks exclusively
Undiluted citrus juice exclusively

stem: Which nursing responsibility involves giving prescribed laryngitis medications correctly and watching for adverse effects?
options: Administering prescribed medications accurately and observing for side effects
Allowing the patient to self-adjust all medication doses without supervision
Withholding all prescribed medications until symptoms fully resolve
Administering only herbal remedies instead of prescribed medications

stem: Which lifestyle modification should the nurse instruct a patient with laryngitis to avoid?
options: Smoking, alcohol, and environmental pollutants
Drinking adequate water throughout the day
Resting the voice as much as possible
Using a room humidifier at night

stem: For a patient whose laryngitis is related to GERD, which dietary modification should the nurse educate on?
options: Avoiding spicy and acidic foods
Increasing intake of citrus fruits and spicy peppers
Eliminating all fluid intake entirely
Eating only immediately before lying down to sleep

stem: Promoting respiratory and hand hygiene in a patient with laryngitis primarily serves which purpose?
options: To prevent the spread of infection
To permanently cure chronic vocal cord nodules
To replace the need for any pharmacological treatment
To eliminate the need for voice rest

stem: Referral to which specialist is recommended for persistent vocal issues in laryngitis?
options: A speech-language therapist
An orthopaedic surgeon
A nephrologist
A dermatologist

stem: Which of the following is listed as a potential complication of laryngitis involving the vocal cords themselves?
options: Vocal cord nodules, polyps, or cysts
Permanent blindness
Complete loss of taste on the tongue
Irreversible hearing loss in both ears

stem: Laryngeal stenosis or granuloma formation is listed as a complication of which condition?
options: Laryngitis
Appendicitis
Otitis media
Conjunctivitis

stem: Airway obstruction, as a complication of laryngitis, is noted to be especially concerning in which patient populations?
options: Children or immunocompromised patients
Healthy adult athletes only
Patients with no history of respiratory illness
Patients who have never smoked

stem: Secondary bacterial infection is listed as a potential complication following which initial process in laryngitis?
options: An initial viral or other inflammatory process affecting the larynx
A fully resolved, asymptomatic episode with no ongoing inflammation
A single dose of a properly indicated antibiotic
A routine dental cleaning unrelated to the larynx

stem: As part of health education, patients should be encouraged to seek early medical consultation for hoarseness persisting beyond which duration?
options: More than three weeks
More than three hours
More than three minutes
More than three years

stem: Health education for laryngitis prevention includes avoiding which behaviour related to the voice?
options: Voice overuse and vocal strain
Deep breathing exercises
Adequate hydration
Hand hygiene practices

stem: What is the general prognosis for ACUTE laryngitis with supportive care?
options: A favorable prognosis, resolving within a few days to a couple of weeks
A universally fatal outcome without surgery
Permanent, irreversible loss of voice in all cases
A prognosis identical to untreated laryngeal cancer

stem: What does the prognosis of CHRONIC laryngitis typically require, in contrast to most cases of acute laryngitis?
options: Management of underlying causes, possibly including voice therapy or surgical intervention for structural complications
No management whatsoever, since it always resolves spontaneously within days
Immediate, mandatory laryngectomy in every case
Only a single dose of antihistamine with no further follow-up

stem: According to the prognosis discussion, what can minimize complications of laryngitis?
options: Early diagnosis and preventive measures
Delaying all medical evaluation for several years
Avoiding any form of hydration
Increasing, rather than resting, vocal activity during acute illness

stem: Which statement correctly distinguishes the TYPICAL infectious cause pattern of acute laryngitis from chronic laryngitis?
options: Acute laryngitis is often due to viral infection, while chronic laryngitis is more often linked to prolonged irritant exposure such as smoking or GERD rather than a single infection
Acute laryngitis is always bacterial, while chronic laryngitis is always fungal
Acute and chronic laryngitis share an identical, single infectious cause in all cases
Chronic laryngitis is always caused by a single untreated viral infection lasting exactly three weeks

stem: Why should antihistamines be used cautiously in allergy-induced laryngitis despite potentially relieving allergic symptoms?
options: Because they can dry the mucosa, which may worsen irritation of an already inflamed larynx
Because they always cause immediate, severe airway obstruction in every patient
Because they are completely ineffective for any allergic condition
Because they permanently cure chronic vocal cord nodules on their own

stem: CASE SCENARIO: A secondary school teacher presents with hoarseness that has persisted for five weeks, worse by the end of each teaching day, with no fever and no recent cold symptoms. She reports frequent heartburn at night. Which type of laryngitis and most likely contributing causes BEST fit this presentation?
options: Chronic laryngitis, most likely related to her high vocal demand occupation and underlying gastroesophageal reflux disease rather than an acute infection
Acute viral laryngitis, since all laryngitis lasting more than a few days is classified as viral
Fungal laryngitis, since all teachers who use corticosteroid inhalers develop Candida infection
A normal voice change requiring no further assessment, since hoarseness lasting five weeks is within expected limits for teachers

stem: CASE SCENARIO: A 4-year-old child with sudden-onset hoarseness and a barking, worsening cough develops audible stridor and visible chest retractions over several hours. Which nursing priority is MOST appropriate at this point?
options: Urgent assessment and escalation for signs of airway obstruction and respiratory distress, since this age group is specifically noted to be at higher risk of this complication of laryngitis
Reassurance that stridor and retractions are expected, harmless findings requiring no further action
Immediate administration of antihistamines alone, since allergy is the only possible cause of stridor in children
Discharge home with voice rest instructions only, with no further monitoring required

stem: CASE SCENARIO: An adult with confirmed fungal laryngitis on throat swab has a history of long-term inhaled corticosteroid use for asthma, with no systemic immunosuppressive illness identified. Which management approach is MOST appropriate?
options: Antifungal therapy directed at the confirmed Candida infection, along with review of inhaler technique and rinsing the mouth after corticosteroid inhaler use
Antibiotics alone, since all throat infections are treated identically regardless of the organism identified
Antihistamines alone, since fungal laryngitis is managed identically to allergy-induced laryngitis
No treatment at all, since fungal laryngitis in inhaler users always resolves without intervention

stem: CASE SCENARIO: A professional singer develops hoarseness after a series of back-to-back performances with inadequate rest between shows, but has no fever, no recent infection, and no reflux symptoms. Laryngoscopy reveals early, mild thickening of the vocal cords. Which combination of interventions is MOST appropriate at this stage?
options: Voice rest, hydration, humidified air, and avoidance of further vocal strain, with surgical referral reserved only if persistent structural lesions such as nodules or polyps develop despite conservative management
Immediate surgical excision of the vocal cords as first-line treatment before any conservative measures are tried
A full course of antibiotics as first-line treatment, since all vocal cord changes require antimicrobial therapy
Encouragement to continue singing at full volume, since vocal rest is unnecessary for professional performers

stem: CASE SCENARIO: A nurse is evaluating two patients with hoarseness: Patient 1 has had symptoms for four days following a cold, with mild throat discomfort and no red-flag signs; Patient 2 has had progressive hoarseness for four months with no infectious symptoms and a long smoking history. Which plan of care correctly matches each patient?
options: Patient 1 is most consistent with acute, self-limiting viral laryngitis managed with supportive care; Patient 2's prolonged hoarseness and smoking history warrant ENT referral and laryngoscopy to exclude structural disease or malignancy
Both patients should be managed identically with voice rest alone and require no further evaluation of any kind
Patient 1 requires urgent laryngoscopy and possible biopsy, while Patient 2 requires only reassurance with no further action
Neither patient requires any assessment beyond reassurance, since hoarseness is never associated with underlying disease
